info.description:
New API management API. Selected authentication/session/proof contracts are source-aligned; remaining legacy management DTOs and dynamic routes are not a complete API inventory. HTTP 200 can contain success:false; inspect the envelope. Role, permission, token scope and operation proof checks are enforced by the server.

Organization selection boundary: this operation has no organization-resource support. An explicit positive X-Organization-Id header or org_id query value returns 403 before resource lookup or upstream work. Malformed/reserved/duplicate selectors return 400; a header and query together return 400 even when equal. Absent selection or a single canonical 0 preserves the existing credential, body and resource rules. Unrelated legacy query bytes are preserved. Request-body fields do not select a local organization. The boundary does not grant authentication or authorize personal/platform resources. This also applies to undeclared methods, dynamic aliases and unmatched routes; it does not register additional endpoints. Framework slash/path redirects may precede middleware; following the redirect must preserve selection and cannot permit personal fallback. HEAD responses have no HTTP body. The five Organizations GET operations are the only positive organization selections supported by this increment.

post.description:
🔐 需要登录（User权限）

Requires a current dashboard Bearer JWT session for organization operations; PATs (including root/wildcard/legacy), relay keys and cookies cannot authenticate this branch. Current database authorization is rechecked. IDs/revisions/generations are canonical decimal strings, never JSON numbers, bounded by signed int64. Only listed queries are allowed once. Use at most one optional X-Organization-Id header OR org_id query, never both; on path routes it must match the path, on pathless routes it must be absent or zero. Duplicate headers/JSON keys at every depth, invalid UTF-8, unknown typed fields, trailing JSON, null required fields, Idempotency-Key and method overrides are rejected. JSON writes require application/json. Names are trimmed to 1..64 Unicode characters without controls; reasons preserve exact text up to 128 characters without controls and must be empty when disabled=false. Explicit false is required and preserved. Same-origin writes use a configured exact Origin allowlist; secure-cookie settings do not disable it; untrusted forwarding headers do not establish origin. Native Bearer JSON without browser Origin metadata is permitted. Request timeout 30s; transaction timeout 10s. No automatic retry. A response-lost create cannot be safely deduplicated. Revision/generation CAS is not response caching. A repeated old request can return 409 before inspecting a consumed proof. Sensitive commands require X-Security-Proof from the matching canonical preview and factor ceremony, under the newly returned SID/JWT. Actual proof consumption commits separately before the business transaction and is never restored after business failure. Proof expiration is checked after locks with no leeway; old SID/session rotation, scope, method, command and snapshot must match. No proof may be supplied to reads, preview or nonsensitive commands. Organization branch only. Existing nonorganization scopes, PAT policy, factor flows, HTTP 200 business errors and proof responses without auth_bundle are retained. Organization OAuth/session/recovery-code methods are unavailable; an enrolled but unavailable/locked stronger factor never falls back to password. Five ceremony starts per account per rolling 300 seconds are shared across scopes/sessions/nodes. Direct verification or passkey begin reserves once; finish uses the server-bound reservation without another charge/refund. Permission: dashboard session only for organization scopes; preserve nonorganization legacy contract. Proof policy: forbidden.

post.description:
Issue a short-lived operation proof after server-side verification. Business verification errors may use HTTP 200 with success:false.

Requires a current dashboard Bearer JWT session for organization operations; PATs (including root/wildcard/legacy), relay keys and cookies cannot authenticate this branch. Current database authorization is rechecked. IDs/revisions/generations are canonical decimal strings, never JSON numbers, bounded by signed int64. Only listed queries are allowed once. Use at most one optional X-Organization-Id header OR org_id query, never both; on path routes it must match the path, on pathless routes it must be absent or zero. Duplicate headers/JSON keys at every depth, invalid UTF-8, unknown typed fields, trailing JSON, null required fields, Idempotency-Key and method overrides are rejected. JSON writes require application/json. Names are trimmed to 1..64 Unicode characters without controls; reasons preserve exact text up to 128 characters without controls and must be empty when disabled=false. Explicit false is required and preserved. Same-origin writes use a configured exact Origin allowlist; secure-cookie settings do not disable it; untrusted forwarding headers do not establish origin. Native Bearer JSON without browser Origin metadata is permitted. Request timeout 30s; transaction timeout 10s. No automatic retry. A response-lost create cannot be safely deduplicated. Revision/generation CAS is not response caching. A repeated old request can return 409 before inspecting a consumed proof. Sensitive commands require X-Security-Proof from the matching canonical preview and factor ceremony, under the newly returned SID/JWT. Actual proof consumption commits separately before the business transaction and is never restored after business failure. Proof expiration is checked after locks with no leeway; old SID/session rotation, scope, method, command and snapshot must match. No proof may be supplied to reads, preview or nonsensitive commands. Organization branch only. Existing nonorganization scopes, PAT policy, factor flows, HTTP 200 business errors and proof responses without auth_bundle are retained. Organization OAuth/session/recovery-code methods are unavailable; an enrolled but unavailable/locked stronger factor never falls back to password. Five ceremony starts per account per rolling 300 seconds are shared across scopes/sessions/nodes. Direct verification or passkey begin reserves once; finish uses the server-bound reservation without another charge/refund. Permission: dashboard session only for organization scopes; preserve nonorganization legacy contract. Proof policy: forbidden.

mandatory_amendments.subject: Exact routes and inputs
mandatory_amendments.requirement: Use the 31 physical route contracts below (27 new, 4 existing organization branches). Correct passkey path: /api/user/passkey/verify/{begin,finish}. Use known target_user_id only; no username/search. Keep S2 matching optional selector policy; no prefix-wide allow. Shared verifier routes retain nonorg behavior; organization branches and server flow lookup enforce session-only.

mandatory_amendments.subject: Reconstructable binding
mandatory_amendments.requirement: Preview command includes organization_id equal to path and every eventual body/path target field. Context={schema_version:1,command,snapshot}; NO public command_hash. Scope fixes action, method and route. Typed canonical normalization/serialization is common to preview, issuer and consumer. Producer reconstructs snapshot from authoritative state and compares all supplied semantic fields. Consumer rebuilds from actual HTTP command, compares stored exact canonical payload and signed HMAC. Client may echo preview but never grants authority. Prospective generation for invite/reissue/initiate, current generation for accept; all int64 increments checked.

mandatory_amendments.subject: Read visibility and locked precedence
mandatory_amendments.requirement: Q07 current members including disabled can obtain only state for restore/leave; Q08 root only. No private platform reason. Pending results include current revision only when caller may perform pending action; terminal/expired/disabled nonactionable results return null revision. Exact historical participant identity is from the event of that generation, not the current reused slot. Lock final users/session/org/members/requests, decide object visibility before revision/disabled/terminal. Do not expose hidden object changes as 409.

mandatory_amendments.subject: TOTP producer anti-replay without DDL
mandatory_amendments.requirement: A01 claim of existing atomic TOTP use is false: model/twofa.go only writes LastUsedAt. Add exact matched-step validation, retain configured 30s, six-digit SHA1, skew=1. Under user then TwoFA lock recheck enabled/locked/factor identity; claim every matching valid step atomically with existing auth_flows unique token_hash via ClaimExternalAuthAssertionWithTx using purpose totp_step and domain-separated HMAC assertion of user+factor-secret fingerprint+step. Never include session/auth_version in replay key; no raw OTP/secret/payload. Markers expire no earlier than max(now+300s, acceptance-window end), existing cleanup retention preserved. Duplicate claim rejects without trying a different matched step. Commit successful use before downstream rotation/proof; downstream failure never restores OTP. Apply shared use path and successful enrollment activation so login/nonorg verification cannot bypass the same marker. Failed attempts remain bounded and transactional. No table/column/index change authorized.

mandatory_amendments.subject: Mandatory account budget
mandatory_amendments.requirement: Five org ceremony starts per rolling 300s/account, aggregate all scopes and session IDs. Direct password/TOTP request reserves before factor evaluation; passkey begin reserves and binds internal attempt row ID into challenge FlowSecurity. Finish checks reservation and claims that challenge once; no second debit, refund or caller-supplied reservation. Budget transaction first performs a no-op UPDATE of the actor user row (SQLite first-write reservation; ignore dialect-dependent RowsAffected), validates authoritative user/session, counts purpose org_verify_attempt rows CreatedAt>now-300, inserts random-token no-secret row with explicit server CreatedAt and ExpiresAt=now+300, then commits before auth. 429 Retry-After is ceil(oldest counted start+300-now), at least1; DB errors 500 no verification. No Redis/global-rate flag bypass; preview/method reads are not charged. A challenge expires at min(start+300, old-session expiry, WebAuthn deadline); invalid/expired flow cannot invoke factor verification. Bounds must hold on two processes.

mandatory_amendments.subject: Rotation and publication failure
mandatory_amendments.requirement: After actual factor success and fresh preflight, generate new random SID/refresh. If Redis enabled, old-session deny fence must succeed before rotation DB commit; failure returns500 without proof/new credential. Lock user then old session; recheck original identity, active status, expiry and current factor policy; atomically revoke old SID (clear previous refresh grace) and create new SID with same absolute ExpiresAt, same user AuthVersion, session version1. Other sessions unchanged. New row may be cached best-effort only after commit; on cache failure authoritative DB snapshot confirmation is mandatory before return. Old deny fence must cover all previous positive cache deadlines and reject late stale fills; final tombstone failure cannot restore old row. If DB rolls back before commit, no successful rotation is claimed and old DB session may remain active after temporary fence expires; do not claim permanent revocation on that failure. After DB commit, sign/publication/response failure never restores old SID; emit no partial bundle, attempt owned new-session revocation on known issuance failure, report failure and require login recovery. Unknown commit outcome gives no proof and requires reconciliation/login. In-flight old refresh may have succeeded before revoke but every subsequently used old-SID credential must fail; never map old refresh to new SID. A late old Set-Cookie may cause re-login, not privilege restoration.

mandatory_amendments.subject: Lock graph and stage boundaries
mandatory_amendments.requirement: Do not nest stage transactions. Existing flow consumer order flow→user→session remains; lifecycle is sorted users→session→org→members→requests; rotation/budget user→session; TOTP user→TwoFA→new marker. A transaction holding user/session/org must never acquire an existing proof/challenge flow lock; new random flow inserts and disjoint-purpose replay markers are permitted. Passkey challenge consumption commits before assertion update and rotation. No org lock across crypto/HTTP. For new user-first mutation transactions use first-write actor row reservation before reads on SQLite; recheck identities after waits. Factor policy rechecks use the same transaction handle and controlled settings snapshot, not nested DB transactions or unrelated handles while holding locks. Deadlock/serialization failure is bounded error, never hidden infinite retry or replay of whole HTTP.

mandatory_amendments.subject: Consume receipt and conflict semantics
mandatory_amendments.requirement: Verify signature/alg/issuer/audience, method/scope, identity and context before CAS. Within flow→user→session transaction recheck payload, policy and actual current time AFTER lock waits. Strict deadline=min(JWT exp, AuthFlow.ExpiresAt, locked session ExpiresAt); no leeway. Overwrite claimed ConsumedAt with final server time after checks, return only after commit. Receipt carries actual row ID/time/deadline/identity/method/canonical binding. Precheck conflict need not consume; after commit all failure paths retain consumed state. Business checks now<ValidUntil after all waits and binds exact full command. Business may finish after grant time within deadline-bound transaction; no false wall-clock cancellation promise. Repeating old request can return409 before consumption inspection; use a still-valid unchanged fixture to prove exact403 CONSUMED.
